<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 37:1">Targ. Job XXXVII, 1</cite> Var.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Amos 3:5">Targ. Am. III, 5</cite> ed. Lag. (oth. ed. <he>יִסַּק</he>); a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 84a:12">B. Mets. 84ᵃ</cite> <he>וש׳ לירדנא וכ׳</he> he ran into the Jordan after him.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 73b:1">B. Bath. 73ᵇ</cite> <he>ושַׁוַּאר מהאי וכ׳</he> (Ms. H. <he>ושוור</he>) and jumped from one mule’s back to the other.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 96b:1">Ib. 96ᵇ</cite> <he>חמרא … שואר</he> wine travels on its owner’s shoulder, i.e. if wine turns sour, it is the purchaser’s bad luck, and the seller is not responsible; oth. opin. (Tosaf.) wine turns sour by transport.
<cite ref="Berakhot 54b:6">Ber. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ עשר אמין</he> he (Moses) jumped ten cubits high.
<cite ref="Shabbat 110a:2">Sabb. 110ᵃ</cite> <he>לִישַׁוַּאר נגרא</he> (Ar. <he>לשוור</he>) let him jump over a ditch.

senses.gloss: (cmp. meanings of קפץ) to close up. Ib. CVII, 42 (Ms. שרור׳, corr. acc.; h. text קפצה).
